description.p: Verbinal is a native Linux companion for the CANFAR Science Portal: launch and manage science sessions, browse VOSpace, search the CADC archive, and look at the data without leaving the desktop.
Its two viewers are built for astronomical data rather than for pictures:

ul.li: A FITS viewer with WCS, colormaps and stretches, percentile and zscale cut levels, an extension selector, a crosshair reading sky coordinates, and blink, linked-crosshair and synced-zoom comparison across tabs.
A cube viewer with GPU volume rendering and an opacity transfer function, plus a 2D slice view with a channel scrubber and per-voxel spectra.

description.p: Marks can be drawn on an image or a cube, labelled, moved and resized. They persist with the file and appear in exported figures, which carry the region's real sky coordinates, the cut levels and a colorbar.
An AI assistant can drive the whole application over a local MCP socket: read what is on screen, point at part of it, and hand back a figure.

An imaging release. Marks can be drawn on a FITS image or a cube; an agent can see the working area and point at part of it; and sky coordinates on modern FITS headers, which were 40 to 90 arcseconds out, are fixed.
A notebook release: cell output is rendered for every MIME type the parser models, figures can be fetched as images, and two file formats that were destroyed by saving them no longer are.
